topic: How does defocused feed array placement optimize coverage versus scan loss in DBF architectures?
consensus_response: Defocused feed arrays mitigate scan loss by directing incident power across a larger aperture, minimizing unwanted sidelobes and interference. This minimizes the need for complex beamforming techniques and increases bandwidth efficiency.  While traditional reflector antennas are more susceptible to element failures due to their single-element nature, defocused arrays offer increased robustness against individual or multiple element losses, contributing to improved network resilience.
